# Tab overflow control can project as the first header action

## Context

Part of the pane-header parity family under epic #13158 — and the direct continuation of the epic's own "tab overflow menu" gap line, whose first half shipped as `Neo.tab.plugin.Overflow`. Family ordering contract (shared, frozen): **[tab overflow, only while overflowing] → [host actions] → [engine set: lock · reload · pin · pop-out · maximize — focus-gated] → [close — always visible, always last]**. Anchors verified at Engine `dev@34499f737b`.

## The Problem

The overflow control is an out-of-collection floating button rooted at `document.body` (`src/tab/plugin/Overflow.mjs:16-24`) — a **deliberate, documented decision**: independent mount/alignment/menu lifecycle, and no tab-button `activeIndex` wiring. That design is correct for a lone tab container. Inside a dock pane header it breaks down: the header's trailing corner is now an action cluster (`close` ships today; the `#17928` family adds more), and a floating control aligned to that same corner collides with it — visually (two unrelated chromes in one corner) and geometrically (the float knows nothing about action-cluster width; the cluster knows nothing about the float).

Two facts have changed since the floating decision was recorded:

1. The flat-action mechanism exists, and the plugin's own jsdoc already concedes the premise: "Ordinary flat toolbar actions can live in that collection because the tab toolbar and SortZone now expose one explicit tab-button subset."
2. Dock headers — the composition this family targets — give the corner an owner: the action cluster.

## The Architectural Reality

- **Plugin (shipped):** pure partition in `Overflow.computeOverflow` (active-never-hidden packing, overflow-only `controlWidth` reservation); runtime half measures natural widths once and caches (removeDom-hidden buttons measure 0 — the cache discipline at `Overflow.mjs:25-30`); the control is created on first overflow and torn down when everything fits (`Overflow.mjs:136-139`); menu selection routes through the existing `activeIndex` path — zero operations, zero persisted state (ADR 0029 §2.4's binding line).
- **Action substrate (shipped):** stable action instances whose `hidden` changes fire `actionVisibilityChange` (`src/toolbar/Base.mjs:314`) — and the Overflow plugin is itself a **consumer** of that signal (`Overflow.mjs:356 onActionSetChange`), which makes self-feedback a real trap this ticket names below.
- **Gating (shipped):** `showOnFocus` resolution (`toolbar/Base.mjs:384-396`) — an action declaring `showOnFocus: false` is exempt from the tab header's focus-gating default.
- **Dock opt-in seam (shipped):** the adapter installs the plugin per projected header (`src/dashboard/dock/projection/LayoutAdapter.mjs:1029`).

## The Fix

An **opt-in render mode** on `Neo.tab.plugin.Overflow` (working name `projectAsAction`, frozen at claim time). When on, the plugin contributes its control as **one stable action item, first in the action area** instead of the floating button — through a NEW **toolbar-owned contribution seam**, never by manual insertion into `items` and never by writing the consumer's `actions` array: `toolbar.Base#syncActions` (toolbar/Base.mjs:469-489) removes every owned action item and rebuilds from the consumer `actions` alone, so a manually inserted item is destroyed by the next `headerActions` replacement (`tab.Container#afterSetHeaderActions`, Container.mjs:221-226), while prepending into `owner.actions` would make the plugin a second writer of consumer state. The seam: the rebuild merges `[contributed items] + [rebuilt consumer actions]`, with contributed INSTANCES preserved across rebuilds — one owner per collection (consumer owns `actions`, the toolbar owns the merge, the contributor owns its contribution), and the stable-instance discipline holds through replacement by construction. The frozen surface: `toolbar.Base#addActionContribution(config)` adopts one contributed action item (stamped `isToolbarActionContribution: true`, inserted at the contribution slot ahead of every consumer action, bound like any action item) and returns the instance; `toolbar.Base#removeActionContribution(instance)` retires it; the toolbar's own destroy retires all contributions. `syncActions` sweeps only NON-contributed action items and re-inserts contributions first, so the contributed instance survives every consumer replacement; `actionsChange` keeps firing with the full merged action list, and contributors self-exclude via the marker — no reinjection listener, no ownership loop.

- **Mounted only while overflowing** (operator-confirmed contract): the action item's `hidden` flips with the partition verdict — Neo `hidden` is removeDom, so nothing occupies the DOM when everything fits, exactly matching today's created-on-first-overflow lifecycle.
- **Exempt from focus gating** (`showOnFocus: false`): when tabs are hidden behind it, reaching them must not require focusing the container first.
- **First action**, before host actions — it reads as the continuation of the tab strip, and `close` keeps the corner-most slot.
- Selection keeps routing through `activeIndex`; width reservation feeds `computeOverflow` from the action item's measured extent while visible (the floating mode's `controlWidth: 40` constant stays the floating default).
- **Self-exclusion invariant:** the plugin must exclude its own action item from the geometry it partitions and from the `actionVisibilityChange` events it consumes — its own hidden-flips must never re-enter its own overflow math.
- The dock adapter opts in at its plugin block; the floating default stays byte-identical for every generic tab consumer.

## Decision Record impact

`amends ADR 0029 §2.4` — the section currently specifies "a floating control"; the amendment makes that the default and adds the opt-in action-slot projection for compositions whose headers carry an action cluster. The ADR edit rides the implementing PR (the `#17838`-style amendment trail).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Mode off: floating behavior byte-identical (existing specs stay green untouched).
- [ ] Mode on: the overflow control renders as the FIRST action item, before host actions; `close` remains last; no floating control exists.
- [ ] Absent from the DOM while everything fits; appears on overflow; disappears when space returns (resize-driven e2e in the same PR, per the epic's gesture-proof guardrail).
- [ ] Visible without container focus (gating exemption witnessed); menu selection activates the hidden tab through the existing path.
- [ ] Replacement witness: replacing `headerActions` while overflowing preserves the contributed overflow action's INSTANCE and first position across `afterSetHeaderActions` → `syncActions` (the rebuild that destroys a manually inserted item).
- [ ] Negative-state replacement witness: replacing `headerActions` while everything fits (the contribution hidden/absent from the DOM) followed by a shrink that overflows again recovers exactly ONE working overflow action, first, menu routing intact — the arm that catches a contribution which only exists after first overflow or is lost while hidden.
- [ ] Coexistence: overflow + host actions + engine `close` in one header with the natural-width cache intact — partition results stable across the action item's own show/hide cycles (self-exclusion witnessed with a spec that would loop without the guard).
- [ ] ADR 0029 §2.4 amendment included in the PR.

## Out of Scope

- Redesigning the floating mode or its alignment.
- Overflow badges/counters, menu content changes.
- The action *semantics* family (those leaves own their actions).

## Related

Parent: #13158 (its original gap list named the overflow menu; this finishes that line for dock compositions). Siblings: #17928 and the pin / pop-out / reload / lock leaves filed alongside. Authority: ADR 0029 §2.4. Prior decision engaged: the out-of-collection paragraph at `src/tab/plugin/Overflow.mjs:16-24`.
